doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Tuition and paying his way through Hamilton
summary: He paid for college with a state scholarship, Catatonic Five earnings and summer jobs, as part of a plan to reach medical school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Right. You didn’t have to go down the hill for too much, or maybe there wasn’t too much to go for.
Down the hill for our haircuts, and that was about it.
Yeah. Do you remember what your tuition was?

I believe it cost about two thousand dollars to go to Hamilton when I started in 1955. And I was just chatting with my wife on the way over here today — the reason I think that’s about right is I pretty much was able to pay my way through Hamilton and I used to make — I had a six hundred dollar state scholarship, those were New York State’s scholarship, and I used to make about six hundred dollars playing with the Catatonic Five, which was a pretty good pay in those days, and a long summer job. I could usually eke out fifty dollars a week so that was another six hundred dollars. So I think my dad had to come up with a couple hundred and I got my Hamilton education. So it’s different today.
Yeah. Very different. But at the time, can I guess that you didn’t feel like you were getting a tremendous bargain? I mean you were working for it and it wasn’t for free.

Certainly it had been my goal to go to college and to go on to medical school and so this was just in the plan and because of the scholarship and the band and the summer jobs it all worked out and so you just sort of — that was the plan and you hewed to it and it worked out and you were glad it went as planned.
